document:
Stop deducting carer's allowance from income based welfare, Currently carer's allowance affects income based welfare. Carer's allowance is deducted from income based welfare like universal credit and Income based ESA., I think this is unfair because I believe it unfairly penalises carers and their families who rely on income based welfare.
  
Treating carer's allowance in this way can lead to financial struggles for households.

Call a General Election, I would like there to be another General Election. 

I believe the current Labour Government have gone back on the promises they laid out in the lead up to the last election.,

Reduce University student tuition fee cap from £9,250 to £3,000, Call on the government to reduce the University Student Tuition Fees cap from £9,250 to £3,000 which the Government has now decided to increase to £9,535 from September 2025. This will put further financial stress on students who are already struggling with accommodation & other costs., The government must consider the fact that Higher Education is key to our nation’s future. A Parliament debate involving MPs is crucial for raising areas of concern such as ever-increasing fees, accommodation costs, debts and an increasingly challenging job market. Parliament must consider the long-term impact on college/university students, graduates and members of the public from poorer background or those with disabilities and the difficulties they face getting a job.

Cap all property management fees and service charges, Property management companies managing privately owned properties have some regulations, however, we think they are insufficient as some leaseholders and tenants are being charged fees which we believe are extortionate as there is no maximum that they can charge., Currently, charges should be "reasonable", which we feel is very open to interpretation. With current cost of living pressures, many people might not be able to fund the fees that management companies are charging. We feel the charges are often nonsensical. If the people could retain these funds they might use it in a more beneficial way to support the country's economy.

Raise the standard tax-free Personal Allowance to £45,000, The Personal Allowance is the amount of income a person can get before they pay tax. It stands at £12,570 in 2024. We would like the standard Personal Allowance raised to what we think is a more realistic figure of £45,000., We think that the Personal Allowance, as termed by the government, has been kept unreasonably low for far too long, at the expense of the poorest, most needy people in our society.

We feel that the poorer majority should pay substantially less than the wealthy. We think that the tax system seems designed to make the divide between rich and poor increase exponentially.

Create a rising tax rate to create a maximum income level, We would like the current tax band system in this country to be abolished, in favour of a formulaic system, where tax is calculated from a starting income of £45,000,  rising to a maximum income figure of around £250,000, in order to create a 'maximum income'., We feel that there have been years of gross inequity in Britain, which have created a tax system that seems designed to make the divide between rich and poor increase exponentially.

Ban holiday companies raising prices in school holidays., Put restrictions on holiday companies so that they are unable to raise prices of holidays so much during school holiday times., We think the government are rightly trying to reduce the amount of time that children are removed from school for family holidays. However, we believe families have no choice as they simply cannot afford to go in holiday times due to companies raising prices significantly! By companies raising prices, and government raising fines, we think it’s becoming harder for families to afford holidays, which in turn could have a hugely negative impact on the travel industry as a whole.

Review of the Royal Duchies, Crown estate and sovereign grant, To carry out a full and comprehensive review of the Crown estate, royal duchies and the sovereign grant. This is in light of recent reports about the large rental income made from Duchies of Lancaster and Cornwall renting land to the NHS and the armed forces., Parliament could pass legislation to alter the sovereign grant and put restrictions on the duchies, and we believe this should be considered.

Raise the maximum assisted speed to 20mph for E-bikes, I want to increase the speed that E-Bikes can receive assistance from the motor up to 20mph instead of 15.5mph., We think it is a small change that will make a big difference to many people and will not compromise on safety.

Change rules so that small cats and dogs are allowed in airplane cabins, Currently government rules state pets aren't allowed in airplane cabins when flying into the UK, except guidance or assistance dogs.

I want Parliament to introduce a law that allows all vaccinated cats and dogs that can fit under airplane seats and that weigh 10kg or under in airline cabins.,

Drivers who hit cats in their car should stop and take the cat to a vet, To change the law: require drivers who accidently hit a cat in their car to stop and take the cat to the vet., As my cat was knocked over 2 months ago. If the person behind didn't stop he could have died.

Protect Cats: Make Reporting Cat Accidents a Legal Requirement, I want cats to have the same protections as dogs, under section 170 of the road traffic act 1988 - so that it is the law to report any accident involving a cat., Cats are beloved family members, and we think it is unjust that drivers can hit a cat without any obligation to report it. Like dogs, we think cats deserve the same protections under the law. We think adding cats to Section 170 of the Road Traffic Act would promote accountability and encourage more cautious driving in areas where cats roam. We believe this change could lead to greater road safety, reducing reckless driving and showing that the welfare of all pets, including cats, truly matters.

Reinstate the hard shoulder on all motorways, We think it is in the public interest with regard to road safety and saving lives to re- instate the hard shoulder on all motorways that have had it removed or have been changed to four lanes., We think motorways are dangerous enough with a hard shoulder but without one they are a high risk to anyone who breaks down or has an accident as unless this happens next to one of the refuge areas (in the event of breakdown) the vehicle will ALWAYS be in a LIVE lane. We think this is totally unacceptable and extremely dangerous.

Increase the UK national speed limits, Change restricted road speeds that are 20 zones to 30 mph
Change Single carriageway A road speeds from 60mph to 80mph
Change Dual carriageway A road and motorway speeds from 70mph to 100mph, The National speed limit which we follow was first introduced in 1965. We think cars are becoming more advanced and better capability in terms of handling and build. We believe it is has more become safe for vehicles ranging from smaller to larger engines to drive at higher speeds without causing any complications.

Reduce the minimum length of the school week, The current minimum expectation for mainstream state-funded schools in England is 32.5 hours, and we think this should be reduced to approximately 28 hours so teachers and students alike can get a proper break., We think this would mean we can get the break the students and teachers so rightly deserve.

Indefinitely detain non-UK national terror suspects without charge, A law to confer upon the police power to detain suspected terrorists who aren't UK nationals without the requirement for immediate formal charge, and for an indeterminate period, to enable the authorities to pursue investigation., We think this provision would allow unfettered access to the detained person for ongoing inquiries while also mitigating the potential threat such individuals may pose to public safety. We think the indefinite custodial mechanism would serve to eliminate temporal restrictions that might otherwise constrain the intelligence-gathering process, thereby facilitating exhaustive scrutiny under lawful detention, thus enhancing national security.

Hold a referendum on a vote of no confidence in this Labour government, Hold a public referendum, The government has breached a number of its manifesto commitments on which the UK electorate voted Labour into office.

Raise the maximum weight limit for Light Goods Vehicles to 3750kg., We would like the Government to increase the maximum weight of Light Goods Vehicles from 3500kg to 3750kg, as we think the regulations around weight limits were set decades ago, vehicles produced nowadays are safer and average curb weights have increased. , We believe that increasing the maximum weight limit for Light Goods Vehicles to 3750kg could benefit businesses by reducing costs and red tape. We also believe that it would lead to more vehicles coming under the Light Goods Vehicle category, which could lead to more vehicle sales and cleaner commercial vehicles on the road.

Institute a maximum cap for the interest rate on credit cards and personal loans, An interest rate cap should be introduced to ensure that people - especially young people at the start of a career - are not trapped in debt and can afford to thrive, not just survive., We believe that in modern society, it is all but mandatory for people to use a credit card in order to build a credit rating. We also think that the UK has one of the highest interest rates in the world for loans and credit cards, with representative rates ranging from 35 to 50% depending on the provider.

We believe that research shows that even small debt has severe mental and physical health effects.

President elect Trump has also suggested a 10% cap on credit card interest rates.

Make onion, garlic and other alliums recognised allergens on food labels, We want the government to require garlic and other alliums to be listed as recognised allergens on food labels., It is recognised that garlic and other alliums can cause an anaphylaxis but it is currently not know how many people have this allergy. We think that further research and investigation is needed to ensure the correct guidance is issued to food manufactures/retailers to prevent allergic reactions.

Change Universal Credit maximum holiday allowance, We urge the Government to extend the maximum holiday allowance from one month to 6 weeks. We believe this is crucial as it aligns with the six-week school holiday period that families only experience once a year., Many parents wish to take their children out on holiday during this time, creating cherished family memories and providing valuable experiences. However, we think the existing limitation prevents them from fully utilising their annual leave. By extending the holiday allowance to 6 weeks, we believe it would not only support families in enjoying their time together but also consider the importance of mental wellbeing and quality family time.

Review decision to cede sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, The United Kingdom has agreed for Mauritius to have sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago. I think this is strategically dangerous, and should be reviewed.,

Raise the income tax personal allowance from £12,570 to £20,000 , Raise the income tax personal allowance from £12570 to £20000. We think this would help low earners to get off benefits and allow pensioners a decent income., We think it is abhorrent to tax pensioners on their state pension when it is over the personal allowance. We also think raising the personal allowance would lift many low earners out of benefits and inject more cash into the economy creating growth.

Stop people raising pointless petitions, intent on overriding democracy., Petitions need to be examined to see if they will actually be debated., Having pointless petitions makes a mockery of the genuine ones.

Deport all immigrants that arrive illegally from safe countries, Deport all illegal immigrants back to their country of origin if considered safe, or country they arrived from., We think this would reduce the costs to the tax paying public, which could mean the Government can house our own homeless and reduce the threat to security.

Require schools to allow children to use the toilet at all times, I would like the government to require schools to allow children to use the toilet at all times., I would like the government to do this as I believe it is unethical to not do it. I understand students may waste time going to the toilets. However, we believe banning students who genuinely need the toilet is unacceptable and must be stopped.

Protection for Leaseholders from rising costs of service charge, Currently, there are no laws to protect the leaseholders from the unreasonable increase in service charges. Estate management companies are scamming residents in the name of inflation and redevelopment. These companies are using their subsidiary to get quotes for service charge-related works., Unreasonable costs such as 8000£ for a telephone bill for a concierge or 20000£ electricity bill for the same where the concierge room is smaller than 1 bed flat.
I would like the Government to put in place a maximum cap system where the service charge is protected by the law for example Considering inflation the service charge shouldn't increase more than CPI rate and if still the increase is required, it should be approved by the Resident's Home Association for that estate

Require all non-essential businesses to close on Christmas and Boxing Day, I call on the Government to require all non-essential businesses, including the hospitality sector, to close on Christmas and Boxing Day so staff can spend time together with their families during the holidays., I work in the hospitality sector and because I have children, I'm forced to work with flexibility on days and so are many of my colleagues. I believe nobody wants to work on Christmas day and we love our job, but would like to be able to spend time with our family over the Christmas period.
Stop publicly funded legal aid to illegal immigrants, We think that the government should stop publicly funded legal aid for illegal immigrants to fight their deportation.,
Make it a legal requirement to call for an ambulance when required, Introduce a law requiring a person to call an ambulance when required. Make failure to seek help when required an offence.,

Give employers tax breaks on wages, Many people have had no real-terms wage rise for years. The UK population in 2023 was 68.3 million. If I gave each person £1 what good would it do? If I split that among 100 entrepreneurs I believe they'd create wealth which could benefit all. , I propose we give employers tax breaks on employees wages so that employers' tax would be reduced by an amount equal to the wages they paid. I believe the ripple effect of tax breaks on employee wages would lead to more wealth & prosperity. I think it's better to have a large number of people paying a small amount of tax than one person paying a lot.

Amend Human Rights Act and review all laws, We would like the Human Rights Act 1998 to be amended to cover “freedom of speech and thought” rather than “freedom of expression”. We would also like all laws to be reviewed from a human rights perspective, and any laws that are assessed to breach these rights to be repealed., We think laws used to be based on actions but are now too much based on feelings and words, which we believe is eroding our rights. We believe laws based on feelings are a very bad idea, because of their subjective nature, and that such laws can be weaponised. 
We consider that amongst the UK population this has generated great fear of saying or doing the wrong thing, and that, furthermore, our Police are wasting time policing feelings and words as opposed to tackling other crime. Free speech is necessary for a healthy democracy.

Hospital Treatment should not count towards School Absence figures, We think the Government should exclude days when a child is hospitalized and receiving treatment from their total annual class absence figure. We think there should be a clear distinction between a child reported as being ill vs a child receiving active hospital care., We think days in the Hospital should not be reported as "absent" as there is no physical way attendance can be achieved or expected.

Include science based Intelligently Designed Creation in the Science Curriculum, We believe discerning visual observance confirms that life on our planet is extremely complicated with species often needing a male and a female for reproduction. In the opinion of many scientists, neo-darwinian evolutionism/abiogenesis is not supported by the evidence and should be re-evaluated., Since 1665, scientific research with microscopes, has shown that all life (creatures and plants) consists of tiny cells which are the basic units of life. All cells are generated by existing cells and require large amounts of information and intelligence. We think these living cells demonstrate a designed plan for individual and corporate life in a ‘just right’ environment. Therefore we believe children should be taught that our world has been intelligently designed and created.

Government to provide information about objects flying above US airbases in UK, Recently, it was reported that flying objects were making incursions into airspace above US airbases located in the UK, with what I believe appears to be minimal effective deterrence. The UK government must be as transparent as possible with what it knows about these craft., I believe any unauthorised incursion of airspace is significant and particularly around military bases, with the potential associated threat to national security. In my view, the government is undoubtedly responding in some way and should be as open as possible about what it thinks the incursions were and the level of threat they may pose – obviously without compromising the operational effectiveness of any ongoing response.

Developers should make new medium to large housing estates fully adoptable., Currently new roads for some of these estates are not made up to a good standard and local authorities don't necessarily want to adopt them., We feel that as a condition of planning applications, developers of medium to large housing developments should be required to enter into agreements with local authorities to construct roads that meet adoptable standards and this should be reflected in amended legislation of the Section 38 agreement of the Highways Act 1980.

Otherwise under the current situation, poorly constructed roads could continue and residents can be made to pay for upkeep of roads if they are not adopted.

MP’s should NOT be allowed to claim expenses for heating., As they have stopped subsidies, I.e, Winter fuel Allowance, it makes MP’s look hypocritical., Parliament should never be saying DO AS I SAY, NOT AS I DO!
remove mp's heating allowance, stop taking from the tax payer, its just wrong

Sort out the mess with the lack of availability of NHS dentists, Make dentists available to all in society, not just the wealthy, it's almost as if we are on the path to nhs privatisation., Come on labour, do what you used to do and help the vulnerable in society.
Sadiq Khan does not deserve a knighthood., This should be discussed in Parliament., Sadiq Khan has not benefited London or Londoners. A knighthood would be a reward for failure.

Prevent the prosecution of veterans for historical offences., I would like the government to prevent members and former members of the armed forces from being prosecuted for alleged historical offences, sometimes decades after the events in question take place., I believe the government owe a debt of gratitude to all the people that have served in the armed forces and should protect them in every way possible.

Increase funding for mental health services for the LGBT+Q community, We think more money for mental health services in the LGBT+Q community-is needed right now. We are worried that suicide rates may be rising fast in our community. , We think the Government should give more funding to mental health services in the LGBT +Q community.

Ban UK exports of pesticides that are banned on UK farms., It has been reported that in 2023 the UK exported pesticides containing 8,489 tonnes of active ingredients that are banned from use on UK farms because of the risks they pose to human health and wildlife.
 
We want these exports stopped.
, Many pesticides are banned in UK because of the dangers they pose to human health and biodiversity. These dangers are as serious abroad as they are in the UK. We believe that allowing them to be exported, meaning that companies producing them in the UK can profit from legislation that may be weaker elsewhere, is hypocritical, callous, and ultimately poses a threat to our own well-being.

Require a licence for prostitution, By making it so a licence is needed for prostitution, we think it would mean that more vulnerable people, such as underage people, people on drugs or people with mental health issues could be stopped from being prostitutes., Prostitution is currently legal in the UK which we think means people who are more vulnerable could be at risk and that it is more likely for young people to be putting themselves in danger.
 
By making it so that people require a licence for prostitution and have to show they meet certain criteria designed to protect vulnerable people. We think it would mean that people may be less likely to choose this and therefore are not in danger, protecting those who are in need of protecting.

Increase Luxury Car supplement threshold to £53k, in line with inflation, Adjust Luxury Car VED threshold in line with inflation. We think this should be done at each budget. We think leaving this frozen at £40k has been another increased and unfair cost to the General Public. We believe it should be applied to all used cars under 5yrs old in a fair backdated scheme., We do not think £40,000 is a ‘Luxury Car’. £40,000 buys a very basic family car due to car price increases, and VED is already viewed by many as an unfair cost to the General Public. We think it is unfair to raise VED rates, but leave this frozen. Inflation rates since April 2017 means we think this should now be £53,000.
 
A backdated/sliding scale should be applied to used cars under 5yrs old to allow for this adjustment.

Do not allow any private companies to be involved in delivering NHS care, We want the Government to protect the NHS. We believe giving profits to companies and shareholders is wasting valuable funds. The Government should put the NHS first., We believe the NHS is essential for the health of the nation. We think we need to fix what we have and bring it back to what it was.

Link the personal tax free allowance to a cost of living/ inflation index., 1 Remove 2028 lock on personal allowance
2 Benchmark to a cost of living index similar to state pension
3 Review and amend annually
, We believe that the evidence points to the fact that not reviewing this allowance in line with inflation etc. disproportionately impacts the less well off as the value of income is eroded so the money buys less goods and services.

Don't reduce the number of trials by jury, There have been reports that the Government may reduce the number of trials by jury. We believe we must retain the right to trial by jury to prevent miscarriages of justice., There is speculation that HM government plans to stop trial by jury for some cases. We think trial by jury goes a long way to prevent miscarriages of justice and trial by judge only is dangerous because some judges are very much out of touch with reality.

Reform the Financial Ombudsman Service (FoS), We would like the Government to reform the Financial Ombudsman Service. We think there should be a much better explanation of when the FoS can help. 
We think the criteria in which you can complain should be reviewed and widened.
, We think online reviews of the service indicate many customers do not receive the help they requested. As it stands we feel the cost of the service is not justified. We think the effort required to submit a complaint to the FoS is very considerable.

Require social media platforms to identify and remove all unsafe content., We think social media platforms can be a haven for misinformation, scam ads, generally unsafe content, and rising abuse. We feel reports are often ignored and inaction could allow the content to run rife on these platforms. We think this can expose people to online risks such as unsafe ads/phishing., We feel that there is rising user resentment towards the laid back attitude of platform controllers and it is apparent that only government can solve the problem. There are concerns that blatant racism as well as victim harassment have been allowed. Besides that, we think misinformation is increasing, including in run-ups to general elections, and what we think are unsafe ads are allowed despite being reported.

Require Property Management agents to disclose all Service Charge Accounts, I think property management agents should be required to disclose the service charge accounts for all leaseholders contributing to the overall management costs of a property estate. I think this disclosure is necessary to ensure transparency and prevent misconduct., I believe this is necessary to ensure service charge discounts cannot be offered to leaseholders who may have a financial interest with the managing agents and freeholders. I think it is critical that this information is made public to ensure full accountability to all leaseholders within the estate.

Require local referenda when introducing new unitary and strategic authorities, There are plans in many counties to introduce new unitary authorities and new Strategic authorities, such as 'Mayoral Combined Authorities'. We think local residents must be provided with information about what these changes entail and be given an opportunity to vote on them., We feel the government has not given local residents a comprehensive insight into how these new bodies/ posts will be elected and by whom. Will it be by proportional representation, for example?
 
What powers will they have compared to the current local government bodies? Does the mayor have the final say on planning disputes, health issues and transport issues?
 
We think it is important that local residents are given comprehensive information, the chance to debate and a final vote on such major changes.

Amend the British Museum Act 1963 to allow for the return of artefacts, Museums are facing calls to return artefacts to their places of origin. The British Museum Act holds that the Trustees of the British Museum shall not dispose of objects vested in them except in very limited circumstances., Some nations have called for the return of artefacts. We believe that other nations can preserve artefacts that are currently in British museums.

Ban the sale of cars with wet belt engines, I would like a ban to stop any wet belt engines being sold in vehicles in the UK., Wet belt engines have been used by a number of car manufacturers but we believe they have a key design flaw which causes premature engine failure. This is because the belt itself can start to break apart and fracture allowing small bits of rubber to drop and gather in the oil sump. It then can clog the oil pump and starve the engine of oil causing it to fail and need replaced. This may happen out of warranty but well before expected.

Require schools close at least a week before Christmas to help protect elderly, This year school holidays in our area started late and schools don't go back until as late as 10th January. Schools should break up at least a week before Christmas to try and reduce the risk of transmitting illnesses from school to older family members they see over Christmas. , I think this would make a big difference to families. Children are one of the biggest culprits of germ spreading and schools one of the places where germs can spread. Most people spend time with elderly relatives over the Christmas break. We think giving time for illness to clear up before this would be very sensible, and would also help avoid a late start to January when there are fewer activities available for families to enjoy. We think this makes sense, especially given that the NHS is more stretched over winter.

Require driving licence suspensions after collisions until investigation is over, I would like anyone who is involved in a serious road traffic collision to have their licence suspended until any police investigation is concluded., I don't think that people who have been involved in a serious collision should be able to drive while this is under investigation.

Require two-week half-term breaks and longer summer holidays at all schools, I want the Government to require all schools to make half-term holidays two weeks long and for the summer break to be at least 8 weeks long. We believe many students are overwhelmed, and need more time off., We believe many students are being overwhelmed by the workload at schools. I think that students should have a longer break so that they can relax and enjoy their life, rather than being stressed from school. You only live once so you should be able to enjoy it.

Set 20mph residential speed limit and require drivers stop after hitting a cat, We want the Government to require drivers to stop and report collisions with a cat, and also impose a blanket 20mph speed limit in all residential areas.,

Set a minimum MOT fee and increase the maximum fee for an MOT, Raising the maximum fee and introducing a minimum charge for UK MOT tests aims to improve inspection quality and help ensure fair pricing, reflecting the rising costs and complexities of modern vehicle testing., We want the Government to:
 
- Implement a Mandatory Minimum Fee for MOT Tests: Establish a set minimum price for all MOT tests to ensure a baseline quality of service and prevent dangerously low pricing practices.
 
- Raise the Maximum Cap on MOT Test Fees: Increase the upper limit of the MOT test fee to align with the rising costs associated with comprehensive vehicle inspections and modern automotive technology.
 
The Government should also regularly review and adjust MOT fees to reflect inflation, technological advancements in vehicles.

Reform the Help to Buy ISA scheme, Allow individuals with a Help to Buy ISA to transfer their account to a Lifetime ISA or increase the maximum house purchase prices to the current UK Average House Price, which in November 2023 was £284,950., Currently, the scheme is capped at £250,000 (or £450,000 in London).
 
The current maximum house purchase price under the Help to Buy ISA scheme restricts access for many aspiring homeowners, particularly in regions where property prices exceed the current limit. Raising the maximum limit to the UK Average House Price would help ensure that this Government initiative more effectively addresses the affordability challenges faced by citizens across diverse geographical and economic backgrounds.

Raise the personal tax allowance to £15,000, We think the Government should put up the personal tax allowance to £15,000. This could help people on a low wage and help with the increase in the cost of living., The Government has frozen our personal tax allowance, and due to inflation we feel that we are watching more of our hard-earned cash vanish.

Increase Public sector pay by 10.5% to improve retention/recruitment, Take the recommendation from the IPPR and increase public sector pay by 10.5% to improve recruitment and retention. The IPPR has said this would restore public sector pay to 2019/20 levels, and should only increase inflation by up to 0.14%., We believe there has been significant under investment in the public sector since 2008/9 financial crisis, and that the consequences of not increasing public sector pay sufficiently are already being felt across the public sector.

Both the NHS and armed forces are struggling for personnel, and we believe this will negatively affect this country and our perception around the globe. The world appears to be getting ever more unpredictable and volatile and we think a strong armed forces and healthcare system is essential to our country.

Read the IPPR's report on public sector pay here: https://ippr-org.files.svdcdn.com/production/Downloads/public-sector-pay-july23.pdf

Require NHS employers to apply pay bands consistently across the country, I think that all NHS banding should be the same, nationally. There have been recent cases of some NHS health care assistants having their bands uplifted, and backpay issued, but not every hospital is following suit. , I call upon the UK government to review the NHS Agenda for Change and ensure banding of job roles must follow a national framework. I have heard that workers in the same roles are being paid on different bands in the same region. I call upon the Government to ensure equal application pay bands for all NHS staff. We believe this is vital to protect our current workforce and keep consistency nationally in order to help with future recruitment into the NHS.

Pass a law on conscription., If a war is declared and conscription announced, all MP’s and their family members cannot be exempt and must be conscripted into the military until that war has finished., All normal military conscription conditions will be followed. MP’s and their families are also to be conscripted to front line service and not some far off position away from the dangers. 

If conscription is so necessary to the war effort, their blood and that of their family members should be weighed as valuable as anyone else’s.

Enhance requirements for farmers to shelter sheep kept outdoors, We want the Government to amend legislation and recommendations in Government guidance so that farmers are required to provide protection from adverse weather conditions. We believe current legislation is not sufficiently clear, and guidance not strong enough., Currently the Government recommends that, where there is no natural shelter for sheep, artificial shelter, such as the placement of straw bales, should be provided. We want farmers to be required to provide structures that shelter sheep from heat, rain, wind and snow.
 
Many of us have seen sheep out on pastures during awful weather with nowhere to hide from the elements. At the moment this appears to be legal. We think proper portable structures should be provided to avoid the sheeps' distress and potential death.

Increase tax-free gift allowance from £3,000 to £9,000 per tax year, We want the Government to amend inheritance tax rules that exempt gifts totalling up to £3,000 per tax year from a person's estate, so that this applies to gifts totalling up to £9,000 per tax year.,

Legally recognise Emotional Support Animals (ESAs), Mental health can be challenging enough let alone when you are shut down or snubbed for having a support dog. I want the Government to recognise Emotional Support Animals (ESAs), so that people with a support animal can't be refused access or services., Many people are oblivious to how much these companion animals can help people with mental health issues to get out and do things. To be refused or laughed at can have an impact on our wellbeing.
 
I have been told I don't need a service dog, and been refused service in shops. This has been detrimental to my mental health and made me think I would be better off just staying indoors and not facing the world. These service dogs can help people to feel normal as can be and free to be able to get out in the fresh air. Without this we can feel stuck inside.

Amend the British Museum Act 1963 to allow for the return of artefacts, Museums are facing calls to return artefacts to their places of origin. The British Museum Act holds that the Trustees of the British Museum shall not dispose of objects vested in them except in very limited circumstances.
 
, Trustees do not have the power to sell, exchange, give away or dispose of any object vested in them and comprised in the Collection except in limited circumstances, such as when the object is a duplicate of another object held in the Collection, or the object is unfit or useless for the purposes of the Museum.
 
Egyptians call for the return of the artefacts inherited from their ancestors. Egypt has preserved its artefacts for thousands of years and can preserve them for the future.

Revoke speeding fines for drivers affected on the A20, sidcup 2023/2024, Cancel speeding fines for people affected by TFLs decision to implement an emergency temporary speed limit on the A20 sidcup eastbound between sandy lane to cookham road. Poor signage, lack of information, confusion and a money grabbing speed trap., Support people affected, reverse NIPs, make change to road signage and markings.

Change child maintenance so parents pay half of average cost of raising child, I want the government to calculate a standard rate for Child Maintenance, based on the average costs of raising a child and require that all paying parents pay half of this no matter their circumstances., I want the government to change to a fair amount that is the same for every paying parent. I believe what the paying parent earns or their circumstances should not be a factor, it should be a standard calculation which is the same for everyone based on half the average costs of raising a child.

Require councils to check all deceased cats for microchips before disposal, We want mandatory microchip checks for EVERY cat - whether obviously domestic or feral - found deceased on any street or property or land, by EVERY council in England., Mandatory microchipping of cats becomes law this year(2024).
 
Many vets and animal welfare organisations scan cats for microchips. We want ALL councils to be required to do the same for any deceased cat.
 
People pay up to £30 per cat to microchip them, to help reunification, but currently a deceased cat can be disposed of without needing to check if he/she is chipped, or trying to reunite them with their companion/owner!
 
We believe this is not acceptable.

Raise the Tax-Free Personal Allowance to £16,000 in the next tax year, The current standard Personal Allowance is £12,570. However, with the current economic challenges and increased living costs, we believe the £12,570 allowance is no longer sufficient for many people., By increasing the standard Personal Allowance from £12,570 to £16,000 we can support average UK workers.
 
We ended December 2023 with an inflation rate of 4.0%. This economic climate has left many struggling to make ends meet, with some full time workers having to use food banks.

Prevent the Post Office from managing an investigation into its own actions., Create an  investigation in which the Post Office has no management function at all., It goes against the principles of independence and judicial fairness that the Post Office can investigate itself.

Limit Mayoral positions to a maximum of two continuous terms , Bring forward a Bill to limit all Mayoral positions to a maximum of two continuous terms., We believe limiting Mayoral positions to a maximum of two terms prevents a candidate from becoming encumbered. Nothing would prevent a candidate from seeking re-election again in the future but this would require that they must step down after a second term.

No more fines for term time holidays . Bring back the two week allowance, Stop the fines for parents taking their children an holidays . Unfortunately not all parents can get time off during school holidays., The fines for parents has created an extremely bad relationship between parents and schools and this has a negative knock on effect. To hear the fines are increasing you will have more parents taking their children out of school schools for homeschooling . Rather than spending time finding people/ parents why dont the government spend more time supporting them. Everyone deserves a holiday for their own mental health and wellbeing and unfortunately if you work you don’t get 13 weeks off per year and can only have time of when suits the business.

Create rights to authorised school absence for family events, I think the Government should introduce authorised school absences for important family events for up to 10 working days a year. I think that current policy places burden on families to choose between a child's school attendance and crucial family events., I 100% endorse regular school attendance. However, I think family events are significant in playing a pivotal role in children's emotional, social and cultural development. I think they promote overall wellbeing and the cohesion of families, foster strong bonds and ultimately contribute to the welfare of societies. I think a balanced approach is needed to accommodate the cultural and familial diversity within our communities, reduce the stress of parents and increase the welfare of families.

Increase funding for state schools and teachers' pay, We call on the government to increase in the amount of funding for state schools, including a fully funded pay increase for teachers, to help solve the issues facing our current state of education., Inflation and underfunded pay rises for teachers have created put state schools across England under pressure. Basic provision like stationary, heating and SEND staff are being cut.
 
We think that pay rises for teachers are paltry when compared with inflation and undervalue the profession. Teachers' recruitment and retention is becoming increasingly difficult. 
 
We think that lack of provision harms children's futures. Let's change this together.

Allow people to claim unfair dismissal after six months, We want the Government to give employees the right to claim unfair dismissal after being at the company for 6 months rather than 2 years., We believe it is unfair that employees can be dismissed by their employer, but are unable to claim unfair dismissal - in most circumstances - unless they have been working there for at least two years.

Allow people to stay in the UK if their employer’s sponsor license is withdrawn, Employer sponsor licenses have been withdrawn by the Home Office because of different issues which are of no fault of the immigrant themselves. These immigrants are then given 60 days to find a new sponsor or face deportation., Most immigrants left all they know, some sold everything they have because they were moving to a new place with their families to start a new beginning. Then they could find themselves facing deportation with nothing to go back to, which can cause mass depression to people affected. We believe that an immigrant who came in legally should not be blamed or penalised for the mistakes or wrong doings of their sponsors. Kindly create another way for them to continue to live and work in the UK legally.

Introduce requirements to improve road safety - car colours and technology, Improve road safety by:
1) requiring all cars to be painted with hi-vis colours (yellow or orange)
2) requiring cars to have technology to limit the maximum speed of a vehicle to the applicable speed limit
3) requiring cameras and AI in cars to help stop mobile phone use while driving.
,

Extend cladding remediation funding to buildings under 11 metres, To ensure equality among homeowners, extend the assistance provided by the Government for remedial cladding works to all homeowners regardless of building height, expanding upon the precedent already set by the Government., In 2020 the Government announced a new fund for remediation of Non-ACM cladding for buildings 18m or higher. In 2022 a further scheme for all residential buildings above 11m in England was announced for fixing unsafe cladding, protecting homeowners from these costs.

Stop differentiating between under/over 25s for Universal Credit, I think that Universal Credit should not have a lower rate for under 25s. I think this puts under 25s at a disadvantage and is discrimination based on age. , People under 25, including single parents, get less Universal Credit because of one sole reason: their age. I believe this is unjustified because I don't think one can accurately predict a difference in expenses caused by a person's age. I think that similar circumstance should equal similar allowance, and regardless that this is about the principle of Equal Rights.

Provide more funding for accommodation for rough sleepers, The Covid pandemic proved that rough sleeping can be prevented and support can be given for those in need. I believe our failure to continue with this support is a disgrace. The Government should provide more funding, like it did during the pandemic to get all rough sleepers into accommodation.,

Fully retain the HMRC Self Assessment helpline , The Government should provide sufficient funding to the HMRC to enable it to keep the Self Assessment telephone helpline open all year so that everyone can access help with their tax affairs when they need it.
, HMRC announced on 19 March that they will close the telephone helpline between 8 April and 30 September every year. On 20 March HMRC halted these plans to engage with its stakeholders. We want to ensure that the changes announced on 19 March are not reinstated. 

We believe that the online automated service can give the wrong answer to the question that has been asked so some people will unintentionally submit incorrect information, resulting in the wrong amount of tax being paid.

Require drivers to stop and seek medical assistance if they hit a cat, I want the Government to make it law that if you hit a cat with a motor vehicle that you must stop and seek medical assistance, either from a local vet or animal welfare organisation., There are too many cats being run over and just left to die because it doesn't say in law you have to stop. Some drivers do, although, many do not.
 
Our family cat Felix had been run over a week ago. Thankfully he managed to get home so I could seek him medical assistance but many cats don't make it home. Unfortunately a week after Felix had to be put to sleep as the damage was too severe. You can imagine the emotional impact that this has had on me and my children. The law needs change.

Allow exchange of Omani Driving License for GB License, HM Government in the UK has reciprocal agreements with the EU, and countries including the UAE, Canada, Japan, Australia and South Africa for exchange of driving licenses. We think it would be a great initiative if Omani licenses are also allowed to convert to a GB License., The Omani Driving license is acquired after stringent driving tests which we believe are comparable to UK and UAE. UK issued licences are already allowed to be exchanged into an Omani driving licence. Many Omanis and Omani-based expatriates face a hassle in having to do a GB driving test again, even though Britons can easily exchange their GB licence to an Omani one.

Require a licence to breed and sell cats and introduce statutory guidance, Introduce a licence for cat breeding and provide additional funding to councils to investigate unlicensed cat breeders. We also think there should be statutory guidance about breeding cats, as with dogs., Currently cat breeders only need a licence if they have a commercial business. Breeders can sell kittens for over £1,000 each. Some have several litters each year and could be making huge amounts of undeclared income. We are also concerned that local authorities don't have the resources they need to investigate cat breeders.

Urge UN Security Council to refer Sri Lanka to the ICC prosecutor , 15 years after the Mullivaikkal massacre of Tamil civilians and a finding of Sri Lankan genocide and war crimes by the Permanent People's Tribunal, the Tamils still lack justice. We urge the Government to seek for the situation to be referred to the ICC prosecutor for lasting reconciliation., There is no peace in Sri Lanka, it is unstable. We believe meaningful stability and reconciliation can only begin once any atrocities of war crimes and genocide are punished. The 2011 Sri Lanka's Killing Fields Documentary showcased the brutalities and yet no justice has resulted. The permanent people's tribunal in 2013 and at least one academic agreed there was indeed a genocide and war crimes.

Allow drivers to reapply for license 3 months after revoked for medical reasons, Drivers in the UK who have medical conditions are expected to inform the DVLA and may have to surrender their driving license for up to 1 year. I believe surrendering your license for 1 year is outdated, and people should be allowed to reapply for their license after three months., The effects of a 1 year ban can make you dependent on others, affect your employment, and place great stress on your family life. It could also place you in financial debt as well as costing the government in benefits if it affects your career. I believe a 1 year ban demoralises you and makes you feel like a criminal. Law abiding drivers suffering from medical conditions consider the safety of others. Please sign this petition to reduce 1 year bans on reapplying for your license down to 3 months.

Make national speed limits for goods vehicles under 3.5t equal those for cars, We want the Government to amend national speed limits for goods vehicles under 3.5 tonnes so they are same as those for cars. We believe current speed restrictions are unnecessary, and impact both goods drivers and other road users.,

Make it a legal requirement for drivers to stop & report collisions with cats, Under section 170 of the Road Traffic Act 1988, a driver is required to stop & report accidents involving specific animals including dogs, but not cats. We want the Government to introduce legislation that makes it a legal requirement for a driver to stop & report accidents involving cats., On 20th April at 0950am, our beloved cat Fawkes was hit by a car travelling over the speed limit on a residential street. Fawkes was less than 2 years old and less than 3 metres away from our front garden. The driver failed to stop. If this legislation is created, we would like it to be known as "Fawkes Law". 
 
The impact on a persons' mental health and wellbeing when their cat is hit by a car can be devastating. Cat owners should be entitled to the same due process afforded to dog owners.

Stop fines for parents taking children out of school for holidays., Government to give an allowance of 10 days per school year for parents to take their children on holiday during term time without being fined., When children leave school with 100% attendance but have missed out on life and family experiences, it is concerning. It is important for children to have family experiences for their own personal development and wellbeing.  The government should be encouraging holidays and life experiences to enrich the education, development, and wellbeing of all children. Not all parents are able to take their children on holiday out of term time, and others are unable to take their family during busy times.

Require safety bollards and speed cameras outside schools and nurseries 
 
, We believe too many schools lack anything in place to stop cars from crashing into buildings. An LSE study showed that from 1992 to 2016, speed cameras reduced accidents by between 17% to 39%. They reduced fatalities by between 58% to 68%. And the effects were seen within 500 metres of the cameras., There have been tragic reports of cars crashing into schools and children. We believe you cannot control drivers however you can implement safety structures to keep our children safer.

Extend planned offence of assaulting retail workers to all public-facing roles, The Government is planning to amend the Criminal Justice Bill to create a specific offence of assaulting retail workers, with custodial sentences up to 6 months and unlimited fines for offenders. The Government should now extend this to all public facing roles., We believe abuse of those who work in a public facing role is on the increase as societal tolerance decreases. We think people in other public-facing roles are now at equal risk compared to those who work in the retail sector and should be afforded the same levels of protection.

Stop giving accommodation, financial support & healthcare to illegal immigrants, We want the Government to stop providing accommodation, financial support and healthcare to people who have entered the UK illegally.,

Let Belinda the cat back in Tesco., Belinda the cat has been visiting Sunbury Tesco for a couple of years now, they have always let her in the store, someone complained and now belinda is being chased away by the managers which is causing stress and upset for her. We demand Belinda is allowed back into store., Allow Belinda back in the store where she has been staying for the last few years!!

Require joint debts be split 50/50 in event of separation, If there is an outstanding joint debt, after a relationship break-up, then it should be made that both parties are liable to pay 50/50 each of the debt, rather than each party being responsible for the whole amount., Where couples have a joint debt, either party can be pursued for the full amount. This can lead to considerable financial hardship. We want rules on debt recovery to be amended, so that following separation each party of a joint debt is only liable for 50% of the total debt.

Remove work restrictions for international students, Amend immigration rules to remove limit on working hours: Revise the existing framework to remove limits on the number of hours international students can work., Alter rules to permit self-employment: This move will align with the entrepreneurial aspirations of many international students.
 
These changes are grounded in principles of human rights and equality.
 
According to some sources the average student's living costs are about £1,078 a month. With high student debt, and a cost of living crisis, a weekly working hour limit, combined with low wages, can mean that students are struggling to meet bare minimum costs.
 
The cap on work limits not just the right to work but also curtails the economic benefit of international students, which was £25.8 billion to the UK economy in 2018/19 (HEPI report).

Require education about assistance dogs at school and workplaces, I would like the Government to ensure that people are educated about assistance dogs and their roles in school and at work so that those with assistance dogs feel safer in school and in the workplace., This could include how service dogs can provide assistance in different situations. For example, people should be educated how service dogs provide assistance during medical emergencies as well as the correct terminology to refer to them.
